=== Overview ===
It is situated on the eastern side of the Umena district of Mishima City, on the western bank of the {{ill|Gotengawa River|Q18988494|qid=Q18988494}}.

It is considered a candidate shrine (ronsha) for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} '''Iwatewake-no-Mikoto Shrine''' (いわてわけのみことじんじゃ), or alternatively the '''Ametsuseketachi-no-Mikoto Shrine''' (あめつせけたちのみことじんじゃ).<ref>[https://shrineheritager.com/unai-shrine/amp/ Unai Shrine] - Shrine Heritager</ref>

Together with {{ill|Sanai Shrine|Q134926924|qid=Q134926924}}, it was enshrined on the left and right sides across the Shimoda Highway as guardian deities of the gate of Mishima Taisha, and has long been revered by the warrior class.<ref name="city1">[https://www.city.mishima.shizuoka.jp/ipn028868.html Unai Shrine] - Mishima City</ref><ref name="city2">[https://www.city.mishima.shizuoka.jp/mishima_info/amenity/rekishi/jinja/jinnja.htm Shrines] - Mishima City</ref>

It is said that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}} often stopped to worship here on his way to Mishima Taisha. According to legend, when Yoritomo found it inconvenient that there was no water for ritual handwashing, he struck the ground of the approach with his {{ill|Naginata|Q546116|qid=Q546116}}, causing water to spring forth—an episode known as “Yoritomo’s Handwashing Water.”<ref name="city1"/>

In the past, there was a pond on the shrine grounds called Umezu Pond (also known as “Eel Pond”), and the area was known as one that held eels in particular reverence within the Mishima region. The shrine was also called “Eel Shrine” or “Eel Forest Shrine,” and among parishioners there was a custom, lasting until the early Meiji period, of not eating eels.<ref name="city2"/><ref>[https://www.mishima-cci.or.jp/796-2/ Eel anecdotes] - Mishima Chamber of Commerce and Industry</ref>
